title: The dashboard Tech Efficiency card gives the report's Show all hours
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have technician A for this test.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed today, on which technician A clocked 2.0 hours.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 2, for customer B, invoiced today, billable, on which technician A clocked 3.0 hours.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports > Technician Efficiency.
  2. Set the date range to today.
  3. Open the dashboard.
  4. Set its range to today.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report opens on Show all.

Step 2:

  • Technician A shows 5.0 hours.

Step 3:

  • The dashboard opens.

Step 4:

  • The Tech Efficiency card shows technician A at 5.0 hours, the same as the report.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R1: “Sales, Sales By Customer, Sales By Representative and Advisor Analysis leave whole internal and no-charge work orders out of every number, with no filter and no option to include them. On a billable work order they leave every no-charge line out of labor revenue, parts revenue, labor cost, parts cost, invoiced hours and worked hours, the way a declined line is left out today: the invoice financial snapshot captures the no-charge lines as excluded, and the per-statement queries carry the same condition. The work order itself stays in with its billable amounts. Every dashboard card and ranking (Sales, Sales by Customer, Top Customers with its invoice count, At-Risk Customers, Billing, and the Invoices card, "Total invoices in range") does the same. The dashboard Tech Efficiency card follows the Technician Efficiency report's default (Show all, S9-R3), so the card and the report give the same hours for a technician.”
  • S9-R3: “Technician Efficiency shows a filter chip "Internal work orders: Hide / Only internal / Show all" (the existing single-choice chip; the chip covers internal and no-charge work orders, tooltip "Internal and no-charge work orders"), default Show all, on both the Invoiced and the Completed tab, so internal hours count as work from the start. With Only internal, hours per technician come from internal and no-charge work orders only, so the accountant can take them for a manual labor entry; a closed internal work order counts as invoiced on the Invoiced tab. With Hide, both the billed and the clocked hours of those work orders are left out. On a billable work order a no-charge line's estimated hours are never counted as invoiced hours and its labor price (zero) never enters the effective labor rate, in the report and in the dashboard Billing Efficiency and Technician Efficiency cards; its clocked hours count as worked hours under Show all and Only internal. The chip's value is part of the report's filter state like any other filter.”
